Every review on this desk uses the same five criteria, so platforms are comparable. My FX Book was scored on its published material alone - including the parts its own marketing skipped.
whatItClaims: A US$200 minimum deposit to start.
Free registration, with account activation by confirmation link.
Risk settings adjustable before the first live trade.
A partner broker holding funds and executing orders.
Withdrawals processed in under a day, per the page.
whatWeChecked: The demo claim: practice account confirmed in the signup flow.
The payout promise: within-a-day wording without processing detail.
The broker relationship: which partner desk executes orders.
The asset list: how many pairs are actually offered.
The registration flow: what personal details the form collects.
The risk disclosure: where the capital-at-risk wording sits.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: Enter your name, email, phone and country, then confirm through the emailed link.

steps.title: Fund
steps.text: Complete the US$200 deposit to unlock the live dashboard.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Set your risk settings, choose automatic or manual mode, and keep the demo running while you learn.

pros: Fast setup - minutes to a live dashboard.
redFlags: Performance language with no dates attached.
A broker relationship described in one vague sentence.
Ownership details missing from the public pages.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$200 minimum.
10 crypto assets through broker partners, per the published pages. The list varies between sections, so check the dashboard after signup.
US$200, funded by bank card, bank transfer, PayPal or Skrill. It is trading capital in your balance, not a fee - and it is exposed to market risk once live.
Yes - signup is free and activates through a confirmation link. The first cost is the US$200 deposit, which stays in your trading balance.

faqs.q: Is My FX Book safe, legit or a scam?
faqs.a: We found no scam indicators in the product, which reads as a functioning AI trading service. The conditions are editorial: claims without verification, conflicting figures and restriction lists that disagree. We rate it safe to research with the conditions in this review.

bottomLine: The verdict on the product is cautious approval: it works, it includes a demo, and it should be used with the minimum deposit while the claims are unproven.
We rate it 4.7 with conditions: the platform is usable, the published claims are not all verifiable, and the US$200 minimum is the right size for testing either.
